co_kiener_s_route.descent_text: Most parties descend the North Face (Cables Route): from the summit area, downclimb third and fourth class ground to the old eyebolts and rappel from them to the base, then walk the Boulderfield back to the Longs Peak Trail. The Keyhole Route is an alternative but is slower and longer. If you left overnight gear at the lake, a gully can be descended from the base of the North Face rappels back to Chasm Lake.
co_kiener_s_route.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Climb Lamb's Slide, a snow or ice couloir of about 1,000 ft at roughly 50 degrees, to within a couple of hundred feet of its top, then exit right onto Broadway. Cross Broadway for about 1,000 ft to the foot of the Notch Couloir; the narrowest step on the ledge needs a roped move or two at fourth class. The rock climbing starts on the far side of the couloir.

co_the_notch_couloir.descent_text: From the Notch at the top of the couloir there are two ways out. One is to rappel the back (west) side and join the Loft route, which leads down to Chasm Lake; the turn-off onto that trail is easy to miss. The other is to traverse east-side ledges to the Staircase, a chimney of about 100 ft and roughly 5.4, climb it to the ridge and scramble fourth class to the summit, then descend the North Face (Cables Route) or the Keyhole. Avalanche and sluff hazard in the couloir is the main concern when conditions are wrong.
co_the_notch_couloir.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Climb Lamb's Slide to Broadway and traverse the ledge (about 1,000 ft, with an exposed section near the start) to the base of the Notch Couloir, the large notch visible east of the summit and left of the Diamond. The couloir climbs about 1,000 ft up to the Notch.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_lamb_s_s.descent_text: Walk or scramble off over easy third-class ground to the Loft and then descend its ramp toward Chasm Lake; the same ground leads to Clark's Arrow if you want the summit. Rappelling the route is possible but is not advised, and the slide gets rockfall, so wear a helmet.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_lamb_s_s.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. The slide is the clear couloir cutting across the base of the lower east face, with a rib of the glacier dividing it from the Flying Dutchman. It is a snow or ice climb of about 1,000 ft at up to roughly 50 degrees, and is the usual way to reach Broadway.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_alexande.descent_text: From the top of the ice, one option is to rappel off the end of the ice; another is to continue to Broadway and finish on Kiener's Route toward the summit. Lamb's Slide, the Crack of Delight rappels and North Chimney are other ways off, with Lamb's Slide bringing rockfall. A party that continues to the summit descends the North Face (Cables Route).
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_alexande.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Climb the lower part of Lamb's Slide until the chimney is overhead, then work up broken rock to the start of the ice at the base of the chimney. A band of snow or ice below the rock step can be steep and hard, so carry crampons and an axe, and watch for rockfall in the slide.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_north_ch.descent_text: The chimney ends on Broadway, where the Crack of Delight rappels go down easily, or you can use Broadway for Kiener's Route or the Window. The rappel line from Broadway leads to Mills Glacier and needs two ropes.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_north_ch.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Continue past the lake to Mills Glacier. The chimney is right of center on the lower east face, directly below Broadway and the Diamond, and follows the large left-slanting chimney above the highest snow on the face other than Lamb's Slide. Field's Chimney, to its left, is often mistaken for it in the dark. Rockfall is common here and parties are usually below you, so take care with ropes.

co_field_s_chimney.descent_text: The chimney tops out on Broadway. From there, the rappel line down the lower east face reaches Mills Glacier with two ropes; it starts on the wide, rubble-covered part of the ledge.
co_field_s_chimney.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Continue past the lake to Mills Glacier. The chimney lies left of North Chimney on the lower east face; the two are easily confused, so locate it on a photo beforehand. It collects everything dropped from the left half of the Diamond, so rockfall is a real hazard, and the rock is loose and wet early in the season.

co_north_face_cables_route.descent_text: Reverse the route: downclimb the technical section or rappel from the old eyebolts, then walk the Boulderfield back to the Longs Peak Trail. The Keyhole Route is the other way down, slower and longer than the Cables rappels.
co_north_face_cables_route.approach: Follow the Longs Peak Trail past Chasm Junction to the Boulderfield; the route starts on the north face a short way beyond it. It is best between midsummer and early fall; earlier, it carries snow and ice and needs crampons.

co_dreamweaver.descent_text: From the top of the couloir, continue to the Meeker summit area and descend toward the Loft; a traversing ledge bypasses steep ice. Late in the season the couloir is mostly scree, and in spring a glissade is possible on the lower slopes.
co_dreamweaver.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Dreamweaver is the obvious couloir left of the Flying Buttress on Mount Meeker. It begins about 500 ft below and left of the buttress on a moderate snowfield that steepens and narrows as it reaches the buttress base.

co_the_flying_dutchman.descent_text: The couloir finishes at the north edge of the Loft. From there, descend the Loft ramp toward Chasm Lake, or continue to the summit by Clark's Arrow.
co_the_flying_dutchman.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The couloir starts at the west end of Chasm Lake, so go around the lake's north side. It climbs about 1,600 ft to the Loft, with a short crux of water ice around 55 degrees.

co_martha.descent_text: Go down Lady Washington's east ridge until it meets the trail at the western end of the Mills Moraine, then walk out on the trail. A ramp on the right of the gully might also lead back to its base.
co_martha.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Contour about halfway around the north side of the lake, then climb talus to the foot of the conspicuous gully on Mount Lady Washington's southern flank; it rises to the saddle between the mountain's two summits.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_abraxsis.descent_text: The route finishes in Eubank's Chimney where it meets Upper Kiener's. Continue by Upper Kiener's to the summit and descend the North Face (Cables Route) with rappels from the old eyebolts.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_abraxsis.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Gain Broadway by Lamb's Slide, Alexander's Chimney or Field's Chimney, then follow the ledge to a point roughly halfway from the Notch Couloir toward the Window. The first two pitches are in a deep chimney above the ledge, reached by some easy climbing.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_conditio.descent_text: Rappel the route with double ropes; the ropes may not quite reach the ground from the top pitch, so be ready to stop and rig again.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_conditio.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The ice is the middle smear of the alcove under the big roofs on the lower east face, sitting between Morning Dew and Crazy Train.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_crazy_tr.descent_text: Rappel the route on double ropes.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_crazy_tr.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. It is the far right smear below the roofs on the lower east face, found between Smear of Fear and Field's Chimney, and it drips from a rock overlap. The ice sometimes does not reach the ground, and the slabs below are smooth.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_smear_of.descent_text: Rappel the route from pins, bolts and v-threads, using rock anchors on the right side if needed; from high on the route it can make sense to cross over to Stettner's Ledges and use its descent.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_smear_of.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The smear is right of the Stettner's Ledges dihedrals on the lower east face. If the ice does not reach the ground, climb in by thin diagonal cracks on its left.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_the_eigh.descent_text: At the top, either rappel into the Notch (the anchor is hard to locate) or walk off the back side and go down the Loft or Lamb's Slide.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_the_eigh.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. The Eighth Route is a broad gully sitting above Alexander's Chimney, immediately left of the Notch Couloir; reach it from Lamb's Slide or Broadway.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_joe_s_so.descent_text: The quickest way down is the Loft. Another option is to rappel into the Notch and continue to the summit of Longs.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_joe_s_so.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Reach Broadway by Lamb's Slide, which exits right onto the ledge, and traverse it to the feature you want. Joe's Solo begins from Broadway in a deep cleft, with the Notch Couloir on one side and The Eighth Route on the other.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_dovetail.descent_text: Walk off by the Keyhole or the Loft, or descend the Cables Route with rappels from the eyebolts; the Cables line is not easy to find unless you know it.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_dovetail.approach: Take the Longs Peak Trail toward the Boulderfield. The Dovetail is a large permanent snowfield on the north face, roughly halfway between the Cables Route and the Keyhole. Climb snow as high as it goes around the right, to about where the first ledges of Keyhole Ridge end, working toward the top of the tail, which bends up and leftward behind a buttress.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_wobbly_b.descent_text: From Table Ledge there are several ways off: rappel D7 or the Crack of Delight, downclimb Kiener's Route and rappel into and down the Notch Couloir to Broadway, or go to the summit by Kiener's and descend the Cables Route. No fixed gear remained on the route in late 2025.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_wobbly_b.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Gain Broadway and walk to the base of the Window route, where Wobbly Baknn Strips begins, high on the Diamond's left side, between the Window and the Obelisk.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_baknnato.descent_text: The route ends on the big ledge atop the fourth pitch of Wobbly Baknn Strips, below Table Ledge. Descent options are as for that route: rappel D7 or the Crack of Delight, downclimb Kiener's Route and rappel the Notch Couloir to Broadway, or go to the summit and descend the Cables Route.
co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_baknnato.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Reach Broadway, walk to the base of the Window, and climb the first three pitches of Wobbly Baknn Strips; Baknnator Indirect starts from the big icy ledge on the third (ice) pitch.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_columbin.approach: From Longs Peak Trailhead on Highway 7, take the Longs Peak Trail toward Chasm Lake; the ice is a short walk off the trail to the lake, in the Columbine Falls and Peacock Pool area. It has a steep start for a short way, then a low-angle slab.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_left_of_.approach: From Longs Peak Trailhead on Highway 7, follow the Longs Peak Trail toward Chasm Lake; the flow is just left of Columbine Falls, a short way from the trail.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_chasm_la.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail. The lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The ice flows come directly off Chasm Lake and are easy to reach from the meadows below it.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_duncan_d.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Look for a smear and an iced chimney northeast of the ranger cabin below Chasm Lake.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_give_r_t.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. The route is a single pitch on the West Tower of Ship's Prow, on the shore of Chasm Lake. Start about 40 ft to the left and higher than where Mizzenmast and Feel the Stern share their opening pitch.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque_gully_le.approach: Start at the Longs Peak Trailhead, on Highway 7, and follow the Longs Peak Trail to the Chasm Lake Trail; the lake is about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain from the trailhead. Skirt Chasm Lake on its north side (in winter the frozen lake can be crossed) to reach Mills Glacier beneath the east face, where Lamb's Slide begins. Climb Lamb's Slide past Zumie's Thumb and go up the gully to its left.
